### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94114c1f269f6b3d885f24b6f4689dce29504574` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b7c1381b5f3ab7cd22e273ea2ed504c1aeee911b` — the merge of head `1f081ab7c11fbe7fb7dd13a9ab24bd62a6aacbd4` into base `94114c1f269f6b3d885f24b6f4689dce29504574`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b7c1381b5f3ab7cd22e273ea2ed504c1aeee911b && git checkout b7c1381b5f3ab7cd22e273ea2ed504c1aeee911b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 94114c1f269f6b3d885f24b6f4689dce29504574 1f081ab7c11fbe7fb7dd13a9ab24bd62a6aacbd4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 94114c1f269f6b3d885f24b6f4689dce29504574 && git merge --no-ff 1f081ab7c11fbe7fb7dd13a9ab24bd62a6aacbd4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94114c1f269f6b3d885f24b6f4689dce29504574
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1f081ab7c11fbe7fb7dd13a9ab24bd62a6aacbd4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/alias-integrity.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-banner-translation.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/system.json, packages/spec/export-origins/system.json, content/docs/references/system/translation.mdx, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/system.md, .changeset/23855-settings-banner-translation-slot.md, packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/en.ts, zh-CN.ts, ja-JP.ts, es-ES.ts, index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts, and in objectui at the pinned `daeb77fc84`: apps/console/src/pages/settings/useSettingsLabel.ts and SettingsField.tsx

Read in this act, clock 2026-10-16T12:21Z: card #23855 body and all three comments (first grade `6212923943`, claim `6213624416`, dev report `6214981300`); PR #23886 body, its nine-file list and the net diff `94114c1f` (the merge-base, equal to the PR base) to `1f081ab7`; the 41 check-runs on the head. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The widening, right.** `platformSettingsShape` gains one optional key, `banners`, a `z.record` of `strictObject({ surface, history: TRANSLATION_HISTORY, aliases }, { title?, text? })` beside `groups` / `keys` / `actions`, built with the same helper and the same history sentence as its three siblings and keyed by the specifier `id` as `groups` and `actions` are. `platformSettingsShape()` is spread in exactly one place (translation.zod.ts:1762, `PlatformTranslationDataSchema`), so the accept set that grows is the platform face alone. Nothing is removed, renamed or narrowed.
- **Leaf aliases, right.** `label` / `name` / `heading` to `title` and `bannerText` / `body` / `description` / `message` to `text`: every target is a key the banner shape declares, and none of the seven alias keys is itself declared there, so no entry is dead and none collides. `description` to `text` is judged correct rather than confusing: an `info_banner` specifier's own `description` is never drawn by the console's banner branch (SettingsField.tsx:273-281 renders the label and the raw `bannerText` only), so the only string a translator can mean by `description` on a banner is the body. `heading` to `title` mirrors the `groups` table.
- **Namespace aliases, right.** `banner` / `notices` / `alerts` to `banners` name a declared key and collide with neither the declared keys (`title`, `description`, `groups`, `keys`, `actions`, `banners`) nor the five pre-existing aliases (`label`, `name`, `sections`, `fields`, `settings`). `alias-integrity.test.ts` judges both halves of every table at runtime (alias key rejected, target accepted) and Test Core is green on this head, so the audit has passed over these tables.
- **The per-app face still refuses `settings`.** `TranslationDataSchema` is built from `appTranslationDataShape()` with `APP_TRANSLATION_KEY_GUIDANCE` (`settings` and `setting` both answered by `PER_APP_SETTINGS_PLATFORM_ONLY`); the diff touches neither, and `TranslationItemSchema` is untouched. Unchanged, as required.
- **The resolvers behave as their siblings do.** `resolveSettingsBannerTitle` (fallback `string`) and `resolveSettingsBannerText` (fallback `string | undefined`) are the exact shape of `resolveSettingsGroupTitle` / `resolveSettingsGroupDescription`: `resolveOptionalString` walks `localeChain(opts)` (the requested locale, then the declared `fallbackChain`, which is skipped for the deployment default locale) and returns the first non-empty string, then `?? fallback` returns the manifest literal. The new test pins a hit, the chain walk, the literal fallback, an undefined bundle and an unknown id. Both are exported through the `export *` barrel at system/index.ts:125.
- **Docblocks and changeset claim only what the code does.** The convention list gains the two paths and its "auto-resolved by resolveSettings* helpers" sentence stays true because the resolvers ship. "A banner without an id has no address here and renders its manifest literals" is true at the pinned console, which renders literals for every banner today. The `SpecifierSchema.id` edit is comment lines only (diff lines 393-402); the `info_banner` superRefine at settings-manifest.zod.ts:596 is untouched, so the specifier's accept set is unchanged as both texts say. The changeset promises the slot, the named-remedy refusals (pinned), the two resolvers and an unchanged specifier, and says nothing about the console rendering the slot; the PR body states the opposite explicitly, and that is what objectui holds at `daeb77fc84`: `useSettingsLabel.ts` declares no banner helper and SettingsField.tsx:273-281 draws `literalLabel` and `spec.bannerText`.
- **Generated outputs match the source.** `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` each gain exactly the two functions and nothing else. The mdx row lands in the `PlatformTranslationData.settings[string]` table carrying the schema's own describe text. The strictness ledger moves by one, the one new `strictObject(` call in `system/`. No committed JSON schema carries this shape (the sibling describe text occurs only in the zod source and the mdx), so nothing else is stale; `check:generated` runs under Lint & Repo Gates, green.
- **The four shipped bundles still parse.** Read at the head: every `settings.NAMESPACE` entry in en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES carries only `title`, `description`, `groups`, `keys` and `actions`, and no `banner`, `banners`, `notices`, `alerts`, `heading` or `body` identifier occurs anywhere in the four files (the only `message` hits are prose inside help strings). The widening adds an optional key and aliases for keys they never write, so the parse result cannot change; Type Check also holds them as object literals typed `PlatformTranslationBundle`. One gap, not blocking: no committed test parses these bundles with `PlatformTranslationDataSchema` (the coverage test never calls safeParse and the plugin's `loadTranslations` does not validate), so the dev's one-off probe is the only runtime parse on record. That pin belongs to #23839's coverage-test surface.
- **File surface held.** The diff touches none of the claim's barred paths: no service-settings manifest or bundle, not the coverage test, not the `info_banner` accept set, not objectui.

### ② Semver level

`minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` matches the diff: one optional key added to a published accept set, two functions added to the public surface, nothing removed, renamed or narrowed. The new aliases change only the refusal text of keys the shape already refused. The PR body's `Clause-②: yes` is the same declaration (`clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes` and `yes (widening)` as one reading). The api-surface and export-origin baselines carry exactly the two new exports each. Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates (the ADR-0087 registration and no-major gates) and Spec property liveness are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1, the strictness ledger file outside the claim's named list: a generated output the claim's "generated outputs their tooling rewrites" clause covers. Accepted.
- Dev deviation 2, `.objectui-sha` pins `daeb77fc84` and objectui was not measured by the dev: measured here at that pin; the console has no banner reader, nothing in this PR depends on it, and the pin is untouched. Closed.
- Dev deviation 3, the bundles control was a one-off probe: closed by the read above; the permanent pin rides #23839, whose surface the coverage test is. Carried as a note to that card, not filed.
- Dev deviations 4 and 5 (PR footer form, a timed-out local run re-run detached): procedural, no bearing on the contract.
- Open question 1, `text` or `description` for the body: A, `text`, as shipped. `description` is a different specifier field, and the alias refuses the borrowing with the right leaf.
- Open question 2, ship the two resolvers: A, as shipped. Without them the convention list's "auto-resolved" sentence would be false for the new paths, and the objectui reader card consumes them.
- Open question 3, keep `notices` / `alerts`: keep. Both halves are verified above and the audit holds them; they cost nothing and name the remedy.
- Landing conditions for the owning seat, not the dev: file the objectui settings-reader card at landing (card body step 2; `useSettingsLabel.ts` and SettingsField.tsx:273-281 at the pin), then release #23839 from `pm:blocked`; the coverage-test extension to banners rides #23839.
- Check-runs on the head: 36 success, 5 skipped (the full-battery lanes and the opt-in tarball smoke), 0 failure, 0 pending.
- The dev's out-of-scope observation (the eleven pre-existing settings resolvers have no unit test) is agreed and non-blocking; not filed here.
